proposals.label: Humanizing framework for AI development
proposals.definition: AI development must be anchored in a human-centred, humanizing framework that protects human dignity and existence.
proposals.inclusion: Passages calling for human-centred, dignity-protecting or human-oversight frameworks for AI.
proposals.exclusion: Passages only about international procedures without values content.
proposals.boundary_cases: The phrase 'does not imperil our existence' borders on existential safety; code here when framed as a humanizing values framework.

examples.quote: we must anchor its development in a universal humanizing framework that does not imperil our existence as human beings

proposals.label: Commercial AI censoring history
proposals.definition: Complaints that commercial AI platforms censor or distort historical facts, such as the history of slavery in the Caribbean.
proposals.inclusion: Passages reporting AI platforms denying access to historical details or distorting facts about a region's history.
proposals.exclusion: General disinformation or election-manipulation concerns.
proposals.boundary_cases: Adjacent passages referencing slave codes without AI count only as context for this theme.

examples.quote: examples of censorship that seek to deny access to the details of our history in this hemisphere
In terms of the Barbados slave code, in terms of the South Carolina slave code.

proposals.label: Well-governed versus poorly governed AI
proposals.definition: AI is framed conditionally: well-governed it widens access to knowledge and public services, poorly governed it deepens inequality and dependence.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages explicitly contrasting AI's benefits and harms depending on governance.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages mentioning AI only as a technology sector of another state.
proposals.boundary_cases: Where the harms listed include dependence on foreign rules, also code AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence adds a further layer. Well-governed, it can widen access to knowledge and improve public services.
Poorly governed, it can deepen inequality, expose critical systems, displace workers

proposals.label: Dependence on externally designed AI
proposals.definition: Concern that developing countries become dependent on AI technologies and rules designed elsewhere.
proposals.inclusion: Include warnings about technological dependence or rules imposed by other states or companies.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general access-gap statements without a dependence framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements on inequality alone are AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: leave developing countries dependent on technologies and rules designed elsewhere

proposals.label: UN Global Dialogue as governance tool
proposals.definition: The UN's global dialogue on AI governance is cited as an existing tool, alongside the argument that national legislation alone cannot govern AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to the UN Global Dialogue or other UN AI mechanisms as answers to AI risk.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for governance with no reference to the UN.
proposals.boundary_cases: The statement that national law cannot govern a borderless technology also supports AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: we have a global dialogue under this organization on the governance of artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Taiwan's AI leadership cited for UN inclusion
proposals.definition: AI is mentioned as one of Taiwan's high-tech strengths to argue for Taiwan's participation in the UN system.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages citing a third party's AI capability as an argument for its inclusion in international bodies.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages discussing the speaker's own AI policy or AI governance.
proposals.boundary_cases: This is essentially a listed mention; it may also be coded AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: Taiwan is a thriving democracy with global leadership in high-tech innovation, semiconductors, AI, biotechnology, renewable energy
She's a serious presence in artificial intelligence and the other technologies that will shape this century

proposals.label: National AI infrastructure investment
proposals.definition: The speaker describes its own national AI investment, such as building an AI hyperscale data centre, and its expected economic benefits.
proposals.inclusion: Include descriptions of the speaker country's own AI projects, data centres, or preparation plans for AI transformation.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general statements about AI's global potential without reference to national action.
proposals.boundary_cases: A statement that the country 'must prepare' for AI transformation counts here if it concerns national policy, and also AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY if risks are mentioned.

examples.quote: taking advantage of our strategic geographic location to establish an AI hyperscale data center

proposals.label: AI driving energy demand
proposals.definition: AI and digitization are framed as accelerating global energy demand, linking AI to energy production and resource strategy.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI to energy consumption, power demand, or energy resources for data centres.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude energy-transition passages that do not mention AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: If AI appears only as an item in a list of transitions next to energy, code AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION instead.

examples.quote: AI and digitization are accelerating this demand at an extraordinary pace.

proposals.label: Need for AI regulation and ethics standards
proposals.definition: Calls for urgent regulations, ethical standards and governance mechanisms for AI, including welcoming UN AI governance mechanisms.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit calls for AI regulation, governance mechanisms, or welcoming new global AI governance bodies.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for responsible national implementation only.
proposals.boundary_cases: Welcoming the UNGA decision on two AI mechanisms also qualifies for AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: regulations, ethical standards, and governance mechanisms are urgently needed
we welcome the recent UN General Assembly decision to establish two global AI governance mechanism

proposals.label: Benefiting from AI while mitigating risks
proposals.definition: AI is framed as offering opportunities that can only be realized with responsible, controlled implementation that mitigates its risks.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages explicitly pairing AI benefits with risks or conditions.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude purely positive or purely negative AI statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Immense benefits' paired with lack of clarity on equity also fits AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: only if we can implement AI responsibly and controlled, Suriname will be able to benefit from the opportunities of this technology and mitigate its risks

proposals.label: AI transforming health, education, agriculture
proposals.definition: AI and other breakthroughs are framed as transforming sectors like health, education, agriculture and public services, advancing sustainable development.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages naming sectoral development gains from AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude sector lists without AI mention.
proposals.boundary_cases: When AI is one of several technologies transforming sectors, code here rather than AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION if sectoral benefits are specified.

examples.quote: offer the prospect of transforming health, education, agriculture, productivity, and public services on a scale scarcely imaginable a generation ago

proposals.label: Technology must not be privilege of few
proposals.definition: Concern about equity and access in AI benefits, insisting technology serve all rather than a few.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI benefits lack equity or access, or must not be a privilege of a few.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude sovereignty/concentration claims about specific companies or states (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Privilege of the few' could indicate concentration; code here when the framing is about people's access.

examples.quote: Technology must not become the privilege of the few. It must become the servant of all humanity.
there is no clarity on equity, access, and applicability

proposals.label: AI listed among global transformations
proposals.definition: AI named alongside climate change, geopolitical shifts and other transformations testing the international order, without substantive discussion.
proposals.inclusion: Passages where AI appears in a list of changes or challenges (climate, conflict, technology) framing a broader argument about multilateralism.
proposals.exclusion: Passages that elaborate specific AI benefits, risks or policies.
proposals.boundary_cases: A single clause adding a brief qualifier (e.g. 'advancing at rapid speed') remains a list mention unless a specific harm or benefit is developed.

examples.quote: Technology, including artificial intelligence, is advancing at rapid speed. Climate change is reshaping our societies.
climate change and the increase in the number of disasters, humanitarian crises, inequalities, and also technological upheavals, notably artificial intelligence

proposals.label: AI advancing faster than collective control
proposals.definition: Concern that AI's speed or uncontrolled expansion outpaces societies' and institutions' ability to assess or manage it.
proposals.inclusion: Passages describing AI as advancing faster than collective assessment capacity or as expanding uncontrolled and threatening security or well-being.
proposals.exclusion: Passages merely noting rapid technological change with no concern about control or governance lag.
proposals.boundary_cases: Vague 'AI threatening our security' without mention of weapons or catastrophic loss of control fits here rather than military or existential-safety themes.

examples.quote: which are often advancing faster than our collective ability to assess their implications
the challenge of the uncontrolled expansion of technology and AI threatening our security and the well-being of our children

proposals.label: AI possibilities alongside exclusion and surveillance
proposals.definition: AI framed explicitly as offering extraordinary possibilities while creating new risks.
proposals.inclusion: Passages pairing AI benefits (health, education, productivity) with named risks (exclusion, exploitation, surveillance, distortion of truth).
proposals.exclusion: Passages naming only benefits or only risks.
proposals.boundary_cases: If only one side is developed and the other is a word, code the dominant side.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence is opening extraordinary possibilities in health, education, science, and productivity, while also creating new risk of exclusion, exploitation, surveillance, and the distortion of truth.

proposals.label: AI as a horizon for progress
proposals.definition: AI presented as a driver of progress and development across sectors.
proposals.inclusion: Passages describing AI as opening horizons for progress or development.
proposals.exclusion: Passages that frame AI primarily as a threat.
proposals.boundary_cases: A progress statement that immediately introduces risks should also be coded with duality.

examples.quote: the artificial intelligence revolution is opening unprecedented horizons for progress across every sphere of life

proposals.label: Human-centred governance protecting freedom, privacy
proposals.definition: AI's challenges to human rights and freedoms, calling for international governance centred on the human being, freedom and privacy.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages demanding AI governance that protects human rights, freedoms and privacy.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude governance calls without rights or human-centred content.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'International governance' phrasing also qualifies for AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE; code both.

examples.quote: This calls for international governance that places the human being with his or her freedom and privacy at the heart of this transformation.

proposals.label: Challenges for the future of work
proposals.definition: AI raising challenges for the future of work.
proposals.inclusion: Include mentions of AI's effects on work or employment.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general economic statements without labour.
proposals.boundary_cases: A brief clause pairing work with rights is coded under both themes.

examples.quote: Yet it also raises challenges for the future of work and for human rights and fundamental freedoms.

proposals.label: Preventing an AI divide atop existing gaps
proposals.definition: Warning against an AI divide layered on existing wealth and development gaps.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements warning of an AI divide compounding inequality.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude domestic trust/rule-of-law content without AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Progress leaves no one behind' without AI reference is not coded.

examples.quote: we must not allow an artificial intelligence divide to emerge on top of the existing gaps in wealth and development

proposals.label: AI as defining imperative of the era
proposals.definition: AI is named alongside climate and inequality as one of the defining global challenges facing humanity, without further elaboration in that passage.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages that rank AI among the era's top global challenges or imperatives.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages with substantive discussion of specific AI risks or policies.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the naming is purely a list of technologies rather than challenges, code AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION instead.

examples.quote: the defining imperatives of our era, namely artificial intelligence, the climate crisis, and deepening global inequalities

proposals.label: AI as instrument of inequality or growth
proposals.definition: Speaker questions whether AI will entrench global inequality or catalyse growth, insisting the Global South lead rather than spectate.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages framing AI in terms of Global South exclusion or leadership in the technological revolution.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that only list AI's benefits.
proposals.boundary_cases: Assertions of Global South leadership backed by domestic AI initiatives are also coded AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: Will the age of the AI become another instrument of global inequality, or will it be a catalyst for our collective growth?
We must ensure that the Global South leads this technological revolution rather than remain a helpless spectator.

proposals.label: National AI initiatives and university
proposals.definition: Speaker cites its own AI initiatives such as a coders programme and an AI university as proof of readiness.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to national AI programmes, institutions or investments.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for international action without domestic initiatives.
proposals.boundary_cases: Skills programmes may also be coded AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.

examples.quote: the soon to be commissioned University of Artificial Intelligence reaffirms that our continent is ready to build the future

proposals.label: Brief call for responsible AI use
proposals.definition: A brief, general call to use AI responsibly for the benefit of humankind, without specific mechanisms.
proposals.inclusion: Include short statements urging responsible or beneficial use of AI without detailing rules or institutions.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls specifying treaties, frameworks or UN bodies (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: If placed next to nuclear weapons without explicit military AI mention, do not code AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.

examples.quote: We should also ensure that new technologies such as artificial intelligence are used responsibly, in a manner that benefits humankind.

proposals.label: AI frontier as marker of global inequality
proposals.definition: Being at the frontier of AI is presented as a privilege of rich nations, contrasted with poverty and crisis elsewhere.
proposals.inclusion: Passages using AI access or leadership as a marker of the divide between advantaged and disadvantaged nations.
proposals.exclusion: Passages naming AI only as a challenge without an inequality contrast.
proposals.boundary_cases: Brief AI references inside a 'two worlds' inequality narrative count here even without policy proposals.

examples.quote: They are at the frontier of the artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies with expanding digital infrastructure and rising standards of living.

proposals.label: AI listed among multilateral challenges
proposals.definition: AI named in a list of global challenges requiring multilateralism, without elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Passages listing AI challenges alongside climate, nuclear weapons and SDGs.
proposals.exclusion: Passages that develop specific AI risks or proposals.
proposals.boundary_cases: A reference to the Global Digital Compact in the same list may additionally be coded AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: To tackle successfully the growing challenges of artificial intelligence.

proposals.label: Global Digital Compact as guide
proposals.definition: UN frameworks such as the Global Digital Compact and Pact for the Future cited as guides for technology challenges.
proposals.inclusion: Passages invoking the Global Digital Compact or Pact for the Future in connection with AI.
proposals.exclusion: UN references unrelated to technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: When cited only within a long list, code together with list mention.

examples.quote: be guided by the global digital compact and the pact for the future

proposals.label: Tribute to Secretary-General's AI governance leadership
proposals.definition: Opening-section tributes crediting the UN Secretary-General with championing global AI governance or international AI cooperation.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages praising the SG or UN initiatives specifically for work on AI governance or AI cooperation.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude tributes to the SG that do not mention AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: A tribute listing AI among many SG initiatives still counts if AI is explicitly named as an SG effort.

examples.quote: a champion of the global debate on global governance of artificial intelligence
to strengthen international cooperation on artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Uncontrolled AI as survival risk
proposals.definition: Framing uncontrolled or ungoverned AI development as a risk to the survival of humanity or an existential-scale threat.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages describing AI as a risk to humanity's survival or as an existential threat due to lack of control or governance.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude military-specific AI risks and generic references to challenges of technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Un-governed AI' listed among existential threats is borderline between this and AI_CRISIS_LIST_MENTION; code both if the passage uses existential language.

examples.quote: the very real risks to the survival of humanity posed by the uncontrolled development of artificial intelligence

proposals.label: AI listed among global crises
proposals.definition: AI named briefly in a catalogue of global challenges or crises (climate, pandemics, conflict) without further discussion.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages where AI appears only as one item in a list of global threats or challenges motivating UN reform.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude lists of technologies or achievements (AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION) and passages that elaborate AI's risks.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the list item carries a qualifier like 'uncontrolled' with explicit survival language, code AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL instead.

examples.quote: a range of challenges, including climate change, pandemics, un-governed artificial intelligence, and energy insecurity

proposals.label: Two worlds: AI advance versus poverty
proposals.definition: Contrasting a world advancing into AI and the fourth industrial revolution with a world left in poverty and marginalization, and calling to narrow the gap.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages depicting a widening gap between AI-advanced and marginalized countries.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages about inequality that do not reference AI or technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: A follow-on passage calling to narrow 'this gap' without naming AI counts only when read with the preceding AI reference.

examples.quote: One is rapidly advancing toward the fourth industrial revolution and artificial intelligence, while the other remains hostage to poverty and marginalization.
It requires us to unite our efforts to devise solutions that are capable of narrowing this gap

proposals.label: AI infrastructure driving critical mineral demand
proposals.definition: AI and digital infrastructure expansion are linked to rising demand for critical minerals, with producer countries demanding local value addition and an end to extractive dependence.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI or data infrastructure to demand for minerals such as cobalt, copper or lithium, or to resource-producer value chains.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude mineral or energy transition passages that do not mention AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the passage stresses concentration of value and technology abroad, it may also be coded AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: the expansion of digital and AI infrastructure are accelerating demand for copper, cobalt, lithium, nickel, and other critical minerals

proposals.label: Prodigious tools if used wisely
proposals.definition: AI and digital technology are presented as powerful tools whose benefits for humanity depend on wise use.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI is a powerful tool conditional on wise or responsible use.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages naming specific risks in detail (code the specific risk).
proposals.boundary_cases: A brief conditional endorsement without explicit risks is borderline; code here when 'if used wisely' or similar conditionality is explicit.

examples.quote: In this era of digital technology and artificial intelligence, we have prodigious tools at our disposal. If used wisely, they can enable us to achieve the desired results

proposals.label: AI's great opportunities and challenges
proposals.definition: AI framed as bringing both great opportunities and great challenges, and it should not lead to marginalization.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages explicitly acknowledging both AI opportunities and challenges/risks.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that only list AI among changes.
proposals.boundary_cases: A warning that AI should not lead to marginalization also fits AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: We are aware of the great opportunities it provides. However, we also recognize the great challenges it poses.

proposals.label: Adopting AI to reshape economy and labour
proposals.definition: AI presented as reshaping economies and labour markets, with adoption necessary to avoid wasting economic opportunities.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI to economic transformation, labour markets or economic opportunity.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude AI health or agriculture uses without economic framing (AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS).
proposals.boundary_cases: National digital strategies framed around AI adoption also qualify for AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: Turning a blind eye to artificial intelligence and not taking advantage of it means wasting economic opportunities.

proposals.label: National digital strategy betting on AI
proposals.definition: The country describes its own strategy for adopting AI responsibly.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to national strategies or bets on AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude global calls without national reference.
proposals.boundary_cases: Generic digital strategies without AI mention are excluded.

examples.quote: This is what the Kingdom of Morocco is working on right now through its digital strategy 2030.

proposals.label: Sharing AI benefits for priority sectors
proposals.definition: International cooperation on AI research and sharing its benefits in health, energy, food and water security and disaster mitigation.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on AI benefits for development sectors or calls to share them through cooperation.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages only listing AI among societal changes.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls to share benefits emphasizing access gaps may also be AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: encourage sharing its benefits in strategic priority areas such as health security, energy transformation, food and water security

proposals.label: AI among rapid technological changes
proposals.definition: AI named alongside social media and IT as part of rapid change, without elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages listing AI among technological changes with no further discussion.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that discuss AI's specific effects.
proposals.boundary_cases: If later sentences discuss AI specifically, use substantive codes.

examples.quote: the rapidly occurring changes at the level of social media, information technology and artificial intelligence are significant and interconnected

proposals.label: AI as accelerator of human development
proposals.definition: AI presented as a potential accelerator of development through knowledge access, health, agriculture and efficient administration.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages describing AI's development benefits in sectors like health, agriculture, education or public administration.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that only discuss dependence or divides.
proposals.boundary_cases: When benefits are immediately qualified by risks, also code AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: AI can broaden access to knowledge, improve health systems, support agricultural workers, and make state administrations more efficient

proposals.label: Avoiding African technological dependence
proposals.definition: Concern that Africa could become dependent on AI technologies, data infrastructure and computing controlled outside the continent, and should instead become a producer.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on dependence on foreign-controlled AI, compute or data infrastructure, or aspirations to be AI producers rather than consumers.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general access gaps without a dependence or control framing (AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that AI may exacerbate divides without mentioning control fit AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: If Africa was to solely consume technologies designed and controlled outside the continent, a new form of dependence could emerge
Africa should not just be a market for frontier technologies. It should also be a platform for design, innovation, and production.

proposals.label: AI exacerbating existing divides
proposals.definition: AI may amplify existing inequalities between regions.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI may widen or amplify divides.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude statements on dependence/control only.
proposals.boundary_cases: Aspirations that AI not become a 'driver of divisions' also fit.

examples.quote: AI can also amplify or exacerbate existing divides

proposals.label: Inclusive development-oriented AI governance
proposals.definition: Support for international AI governance that is inclusive, responsible and development-oriented.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for international AI governance.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national institution-building unrelated to AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: If UN bodies are named, add AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: Benin is in favor of international AI governance that's inclusive, responsible, and development-oriented

proposals.label: Preparing youth through critical-thinking education
proposals.definition: AI transformation calls for education that equips young people with critical thinking and creativity, and for listening to youth.
proposals.inclusion: Passages linking AI to youth, education, critical thinking or intergenerational responsibility.
proposals.exclusion: Workforce reskilling without youth/education focus (use AI_ECONOMY_LABOR).
proposals.boundary_cases: Youth mentioned only as future generations without education content go to other codes.

examples.quote: we should endow our young people with the means to develop their critical thinking skills and their creativity

proposals.label: Extreme AI risks require responsibility
proposals.definition: Reference to debates on the most extreme risks of AI as a reminder that progress cannot be divorced from responsibility.
proposals.inclusion: Passages referencing extreme, catastrophic or frontier AI risks.
proposals.exclusion: Everyday harms such as jobs or bias.
proposals.boundary_cases: A brief nod to extreme-risk debates still counts here.

examples.quote: The current debates about the most extreme risks of AI remind us that technological progress cannot be divorced from responsibility.

proposals.label: Enthusiasm alongside real concerns
proposals.definition: AI transforming life and work with enthusiasm paired with very real concerns.
proposals.inclusion: Passages pairing AI's possibilities with concerns.
proposals.exclusion: One-sided mentions.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of transformation of work may also take AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.

examples.quote: The enthusiasm they give rise to also goes hand in hand with the very real concerns.

proposals.label: Human beings at the heart of decisions
proposals.definition: Human-centred principle: people at the heart of decision-making on AI, protecting rights, security and well-being.
proposals.inclusion: Passages advocating a human-centred approach and protection of rights in the face of AI.
proposals.exclusion: Explicit human control over AI systems (use AI_HUMAN_CONTROL_OVERSIGHT).
proposals.boundary_cases: Generic humanist principles count when stated in response to AI transformation.

examples.quote: Human beings should be at the heart of all of our decision making.

proposals.label: Welcoming UN AI resolutions and Pact
proposals.definition: Welcoming UN outcomes on AI and digital cooperation: the Pact for the Future, Global Digital Compact, and the first GA resolution on AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages welcoming UN agreements, resolutions or compacts that address AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude UN reform or Secretary-General selection remarks without AI content.
proposals.boundary_cases: A summary of a UN summit agenda naming AI as one item counts here if the UN outcome is the focus.

examples.quote: the first-ever resolution on artificial intelligence, to promote safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development
ensuring that we make artificial intelligence, a technology that benefits all

proposals.label: AI accelerating development and state capacity
proposals.definition: AI and digital transition as opportunities to accelerate development and improve state capacities.
proposals.inclusion: Include claims that AI can accelerate development or serve sustainable development.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages focused only on access gaps.
proposals.boundary_cases: Conditional benefit statements ('only if we bridge the divide') are coded here and AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: The digital transition and artificial intelligence also offer new opportunities to accelerate development and improve the capacities of our states.

proposals.label: Bridge divide via technology sharing
proposals.definition: Conditioning AI's benefits on bridging the digital divide, technology sharing and building developing-country capacities.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for technology sharing, capacity-building or bridging the digital divide in connection with AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general development finance calls unrelated to technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: If only the gap is described without a remedy, prefer AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: bridge the digital divide, facilitate technology sharing, and build the capacities of developing countries

proposals.label: Calls for binding international AI regulation
proposals.definition: Speaker calls for international rules, binding standards, charters or global governance of AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages demanding binding universal standards, a global charter, or international governance of AI use.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that only list AI as an investment area without any governance or regulation claim.
proposals.boundary_cases: Support for UN-led governance counts here and also in AI_UN_ROLE if a specific UN instrument is named.

examples.quote: We call for the adoption of binding universal standards so as to regulate the use of AI and digital technologies
We propose also the establishment of a global charter for digital governance and ethical artificial intelligence so that human rights are protected in the digital sphere.
We also call for international governance of artificial intelligence in outer space.

proposals.label: Global Digital Compact and UN AI efforts
proposals.definition: Speaker welcomes or urges implementation of UN instruments on AI, especially the Global Digital Compact and Pact for the Future, or UN efforts on AI governance.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit references to the Global Digital Compact, Pact for the Future or UN efforts to govern AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic support for multilateralism that does not connect to AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: A passage welcoming the GDC as regulating AI counts even when the main claim is about regulation generally.

examples.quote: my country welcomes the adoption of the Global Digital Compact (see resolution 79/1), which should enable better use of that technological advance
The Global Digital Compact must become a reality.

examples.text: “The world is changing. It is therefore up to us to take the appropriate decisions and orientations to make it better, for the well-being of our populations. We can get there so long as we can strengthen our solidarity in order to address our common challenges together. In this era of digital technology and artificial intelligence, we have prodigious tools at our disposal. If used wisely, they can enable us to achieve the desired results to ensure the survival of humankind and guarantee a better future.”

The threat of nuclear weapons is another source of grave concern for humankind. The international community needs to prioritize dialogue in order to de-escalate tensions and prevent the threat of nuclear weapons. We should also ensure that new technologies such as artificial intelligence are used responsibly, in a manner that benefits humankind.

This session is being held in a critical global context, marked by many challenges related to geopolitical tensions, climate change, poverty, migration, terrorism, hate speech, pandemics and natural disasters. Nevertheless, the current pace of scientific and technological progress may constitute a source of optimism, provided that the current challenges lead to international cooperation and solidarity in the promotion of scientific research, including artificial intelligence, and encourage sharing its benefits in strategic priority areas such as health security, energy transformation, food and water security, modern technologies and natural-disaster mitigation.

In addition to facing security and climate challenges, the world is being shaped by a technological revolution for which few countries are prepared. Artificial intelligence holds great promise for our societies, but it can also pose a number of threats and lead to abuses, owing to the lack of international regulations governing its use. Consequently, it is incumbent upon us to ensure that that revolution does not exacerbate inequalities or lead to the digital disadvantage of part of humankind, but that, on the contrary, it promotes the progress and well-being of all. It is for that reason that my country welcomes the adoption of the Global Digital Compact (see resolution 79/1), which should enable better use of that technological advance, in the service of the progress of all nations.

Mr. President, Your Excellencies, we stand at the brink of a precipice. International law, as we know it, is challenged in an unprecedented manner. 80 years since the United Nations emerged out of World War II. Today, we stand before drastic, unpredictable geopolitical shifts, instability that appears to spiral, and an uncharted landscape that seems resistant to the international order and norms as we know them. We are witnessing devastating wars, and unimaginable humanitarian catastrophe and human suffering, blatant violations of international law and international humanitarian law that bring our system to its knees. We stand before the rise of use of force against sovereign states that constantly escalate and expand, threatening regional security and stability. States are sponsoring Malayan actors to destabilize, disrupting critical maritime routes. The use of new means of warfare is rising without even the most basic safeguards in place. Global security is constantly undermined. And climate change is looming, threatening livelihoods, economies, creating new migration routes, and inequalities are becoming embedded. Our world is changing rapidly. And while there can be no doubt that the United Nations has served a noble cause and that together we have achieved tremendous progress, at this critical moment of inflection, we have a responsibility to recognize the shortcomings, to admit that we have lagged behind, that we have failed along the way, and these admissions need to steer us into action. We must urgently evolve to be fit to effectively address the immense, complex challenges we are faced with. Ladies and gentlemen, this is our moment of responsibility. Collective responsibility and individual state responsibility inextricably linked and mutually reinforcing. The scale and nature of the challenges we face require both. Better together is the theme of this year's assembly, but beyond better, we are also stronger together, more resilient together. This is a moment to renew our collective commitment and stand firmly and boldly in support of multilateralism and international law.

We stand convinced that we need to build a better world in which we would live better together. This session, of course, and naturally, represents an opportunity to celebrate 80 years of achievements by our organization in the service of humanity as a whole and in various fields. Madam President, Excellencies, the condition of today's world is more complicated, more dangerous than ever. More uneven in its human development, more integrated, yet more disparate and desperate. Civilized discourse tempered with patience and calm has given way to a bellicosity of language shouted across continents and oceans, designed presumably to satisfy nativist longings in the breasts of those who think that, despite their good fortune, relatively, they have been grievously wronged by some dark and hidden forces. Can none of these persons pause and reflect upon the question posed and answered by all the world's great religions, but in particular, through the words of the Hebrew prophet Micah, What does the Lord require of us? To do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with our God. The intractable problems facing humanity cannot be solved by any one nation unilaterally. A mature multilateralism is required to address satisfactorily rampaging climate change in the age of the Anthropocene. To resolve the threats posed by nuclear weapons and their further spread. To tackle successfully the growing challenges of artificial intelligence. To achieve the 17 Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. be guided by the global digital compact and the pact for the future and to reshape global governance more inclusively. It is thus of the highest importance for this august body, the United Nations, and the overwhelming majority of nation states within it, to continue our efforts to persuade the powerful to act equitably, honorably, and multilaterally to tackle efficaciously the extent and looming challenges facing the global community.

Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, we must also prepare for the next great transformation, that of artificial intelligence, AI, which could become one of the greatest accelerators of human development. Mr. President, allow me first to congratulate you on your election to the presidency of the 81st session and to assure you of Belize's full support. For more than 80 years, this organization has done what no single nation could. It has held back conflict where it could and named it where it could not. It has given the powerless a language of rights. It has built one instrument at a time, the body of international law on which every state in this hall, large or small, now depends. It has survived a Cold War, as it has division and doubt, because each generation that comes through its doors understood the same simple truth. No nation, however powerful, can secure peace, prosperity, or a habitable nation on its own. That was true in 1945. It is true today. The chapter is hope. It speaks to our common humanity. It speaks to the rule of law, to the dignity of every person, to the sovereign equality of states, and to our duty to keep the peace. These are not the words of one region or one era. They belong to all of us. They bind all of us. Few in this hall would question that mission. But let us be honest with one another. Not one of us could fault the people we represent for questioning its delivery. The world is on course to exceed the 1.5 degree threshold. Rising seas threaten coastlines, communities, and for some members, the very territory of the state. The loss of biodiversity weakens the forest, reefs and mangroves on which our economies depend. These pressures unfold alongside armed conflict, disrupted supply chains, declining official development assistance, and rising debt. Households face higher food and energy bills. Artificial intelligence adds a further layer. Well-governed, it can widen access to knowledge and improve public services.

Poorly governed, it can deepen inequality, expose critical systems, displace workers, and leave developing countries dependent on technologies and rules designed elsewhere. We have the Law of the Sea Regime and the Declaration on Sea Level Rise. And we have a global dialogue under this organization on the governance of artificial intelligence. the United Nations is doing its part. The question before us is whether we will use these tools, whether we have the will to deliver. Mr. President, Belize is determined to do so. We are committed to the Sustainable Development Goals, and we are making measurable progress. Multidimensional poverty stands at 19.1% and unemployment at 1.9%. Public debt has been brought down to 66.6% of GDP and for the first time in a generation, it is on a path of sustainable development. These figures are not abstractions. They are beliefs that work, families with greater purchasing power, and a government with room to invest in the future. Vamos bien. We are doing well, but we have further to go. That is the purpose of the next phase of our national strategy, to create jobs, reduce vulnerability, reduce exposure to imported energy, protect the ecosystems, and equip Belizeans to compete in a changing economy. Mr. President, for 55 years after independence, Belize continues to pursue the peaceful settlement of its territorial disputes with Guatemala and with Honduras. Belize has chosen and will always choose law over force. Belize informs this assembly of a serious breach of international law committed on the night of 23rd September 2026 when a Guatemalan military aircraft entered Belize's sovereign airspace and intentionally disabled its transponder. This act violates the Chicago Convention on International Civil Aviation, customary norms governing state aircraft, and the inviolability of territorial sovereignty protected under Article 2.4 of the United Nations. This incursion is not an isolated one. It forms a part of a continuing pattern in which Guatemalan state vessels and personnel operate unlawfully in Belizean territorial waters of the Sarstoon River, which forms part of Belize's border with Guatemala, in defiance of obligations binding on both parties to refrain from any action capable of aggravating or extending the dispute presently before the International Court of Justice. The case is scheduled for hearing in February 2027. Guatemala's conduct risk prejudicing the court's authority and undermines the principle of peaceful settlement of disputes enshrined in Article 33 of the Charter.

Mr. President, Excellencies, my friends, we meet at a time when the obstacles confronting human progress are multiplying. Obstacles to peace, obstacles to food and clean water, obstacles to finance, medicine, and education, obstacles to movement and opportunity, obstacles to technology, to the knowledge and infrastructure needed to use it. And increasingly, obstacles between nations, between communities, and between people who no longer agree on the same facts or trust the same institutions. The climate crisis is accelerating. Even though the science is clear enough for us to act, and many of the solutions are already known. And despite unprecedented global wealth, millions remain without reliable access to food, water, health, or shelter. These challenges, my friends, are creating the polycrises of which we constantly speak. And at the same time, new challenges are emerging. And yet the cooperation needed to confront these challenges is under strain. It is why I believe the theme this year is so apt, restoring trust. Managing transformation, a United Nation that delivers for all. The theme reminds us that we have institutions created to preserve peace, to advance development, and yes, to protect human dignity. The institutions are these very United Nations. We have shared principles grounded in sovereign equality and in the recognition that our responsibilities extend beyond borders. The Reality is that we understand that there is regrettably enough for us to be able to invest in prevention rather than waiting to finance reconstruction. We equally now understand enough about the rapid development of AI to know that as we welcome its promise, we must anchor its development in a universal humanizing framework that does not imperil our existence as human beings. The failure, my friends, to address these challenges, therefore, is not one simply of knowledge or capacity. It is our repeated failure to convert what we know into what we do, to turn principle into practice and global capacity into solidarity. So beneath our many crises lies yet another one. We in the Caribbean understand something about the necessity of living together. We had no choice. Barbadian novelist and essayist George Laming once described the Caribbean as perhaps the first global experiment in human history. Bringing together and I quote every branch of the human family. From the indigenous peoples of the Americas to the diverse peoples from Africa, Europe, and Asia. It is as though that we through this torturous and shared history of migration, conquest, slavery, and the difficult work of constructing a common national and regional destiny that we give the world an example to follow. And to you, Mr. President, Barbados extends its warm congratulations.

But two years after its adoption, negotiations on Security Council reform are still ongoing. The decision so urgently needed has yet to be made. President of the General Assembly, United Nations Secretary-General, Heads of State and Government, Your Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, Switzerland is a country of mountains, valleys and different languages. Mr. President, Excellencies, as the UN Secretary General reminded us a few years ago, the United Nations is a product of hope. 81 years after its birth, that hope is being tested. We expect international law, including the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, to be applied consistently. The climate emergency demands action, development demands investment, and peace and humanitarian crises demand solidarity. As the mandate of the outgoing Secretary-General, His Excellency Antonio Guterres, draws to a close, I should like on behalf of my president, His Excellency Ismael Omar Guelleh, to express our profound gratitude for his years of service to the UN. Thank you.

Excellency Khalilur Rahman, President of the 81st session of the United General Assembly. Excellency Antonio Guterres, Secretary General of the United Nations. Mr. Secretary-General, The more I reflect on the theme of this session of the General Assembly, "Restoring trust and managing transformation: a United Nations that delivers for all," the more convinced I become of the wisdom of that choice. Without mutual trust, peace and security cannot take root among States. nor can cooperation among them flourish. More than 80 years ago, the United Nations was founded on the promise that the force of law would replace the law of force. Yet, we still live in a world of multiplying wars and conflicts, a world that spends more on armaments than on development. Civilians remain the primary victims. while millions face displacement, hunger, and deprivation. The problem is not the absence of rules. It is their selective application, if not their outright non-application. The sovereignty of states cannot be untouchable in one place and negotiable in another, nor can the rules of international law apply to some but not to others. Restoring trust requires respect for international law. It requires investment in preventing conflicts before they erupt and in development before poverty and deprivation become a source of violence, extremism, and terrorism. Development, too, is a matter of peace. There can be no sustainable peace in a world of widening economic disparities. where some states spend more on servicing their debt than on the health of their citizens and the education of their children. This does not absolve developing countries of the responsibility to undertake reform, combat corruption and build institutions. But those efforts require a fairer and more equitable international economic order, one that offers them genuine opportunities to advance. Mr. President, our shared responsibility is equally evident in the face of the profound transformations our world is undergoing. Climate change threatens the lives and livelihoods of millions. Those countries that have contributed least to it bear its gravest consequences. This calls for equitable adaptation, finance, and technology transfer. At the same time, the artificial intelligence revolution is opening unprecedented horizons for progress across every sphere of life.

Yet it also raises challenges for the future of work and for human rights and fundamental freedoms. This calls for international governance that places the human being with his or her freedom and privacy at the heart of this transformation. Above all, we must not allow an artificial intelligence divide to emerge on top of the existing gaps in wealth and development. Restoring trust requires that every individual feel that the law protects them, that development do not exclude them, and that progress leaves no one behind. Mr. President, if restoring trust is a challenge facing our world today, for Lebanon, it is not a mere slogan. Just as managing transformation is not an option up for debate. Together, they constitute the very essence of the mission we pledged before our people, before our Arab brothers, and before the entire world on the day I was entrusted with leading the government of Lebanon. We assumed this responsibility at a time when our country faced three existential challenges. The first was to regain the trust of its people after the financial collapse and the Beirut port explosion and the tragedies and wounds they left behind. The second was to reclaim its national decision-making, so that no authority stands above that of the state, no weapons exist outside its armed forces, and no decision on war and peace is taken outside its constitutional institutions. The third was to recover all of its territory from Israeli occupation and to extend its sovereignty over the entirety of its national soil through its own forces in implementation of the Taif Agreement and in sincere respect for the relevant international resolutions on Lebanon. Foremost among these is Resolution 1701, which remains to this day a fundamental point of reference governing relations between Lebanon and Israel. Trust rebuilt, decision-making reclaimed, land liberated, that is the equation for Lebanon's recovery. These are not three separate challenges. They are three facets of a single cause. Restoring a state that its citizens trust, that is master of its own decisions, and that exercises sovereignty over the whole of its territory.

Madame President, this brings me to a question that is very dear to my heart. What kind of world do we want to bequeath to future generations? We often talk about young people as if they came from the future. Truth be told, they are already shaping the present. Therefore, it is incumbent upon us to ask ourselves if we're really preparing a future that is going to earn their trust. My personal experience has done nothing but reinforce this conviction. This year, I had the privilege of succeeding His Majesty King Carl Gustaf of Sweden as honorary chair of the World Scout Foundation. My longstanding commitment to the Scout movement has taught me a great deal about the power of intergenerational dialogue, solidarity, and the values of the Scout movement. also taught me something absolutely fundamental. Placing our trust in young people means giving them responsibilities, allowing them to take action. They're growing up in a world in which there are extraordinary possibilities, but it's also a world where uncertainty runs deep. Artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies are already transforming our way of life and the way in which we work. The enthusiasm they give rise to also goes hand in hand with the very real concerns. The current debates about the most extreme risks of AI remind us that technological progress cannot be divorced from responsibility. As we confront these transformations, we should endow our young people with the means to develop their critical thinking skills and their creativity. And this is exactly what education is supposed to do, transmit knowledge and competencies, but also to teach young people to call things into question, to open up to others and to shoulder your responsibilities. Against this backdrop, I believe that we should have one guiding principle. Human beings should be at the heart of all of our decision making. We must protect the rights, security and the well-being of all. We should also listen to young people, ask them what we can build working hand in hand.

At this very moment, my government is introducing legal and institutional measures to better protect our forests and the immediate living environment of indigenous people and tribal communities. Their knowledge and participation are important at all stages of development. Last year at this rostrum, I noted that Suriname is diversity. And at a time when diversity is too often manipulated as a source of division, Suriname has chosen the path to recognize the distinct histories of its people while strengthening their unity and their shared responsibility for the future. Our experience affirms that diversity, when grounded in equality, mutual respect, and meaningful participation, is not an adversity. It is a source of national resilience and prosperity. And this process is also relevant for the global community. Mr. President, the development of Suriname's offshore natural resources including oil and gas, will present significant opportunities to accelerate national development and improve the well-being of our people. Yet we are equally conscious that oil and gas cannot and should not become the only foundation of our economy. Our approach is therefore clear. Your Excellency, Dr. Halil Rahman, President of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, Your Excellency Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations, Excellencies, Heads of State and Government, distinguished delegates, good afternoon. Mr. President, about 80 years ago, The United Nations was founded in San Francisco on a simple but enduring principle: that nations can prevent war and advance peace through trust, collective action, and respect the UN Charter. Today, war and insecurity are not only existential threats to our survival, but a range of challenges, including climate change, pandemics, un-governed artificial intelligence, and energy insecurity, just to mention a few.
